summary: The medium finding from the previous round is fully closed: .vibepro/config.json at 2f200bf2 has exactly one story-vibepro-task-atomic-repo-control-contract key, the retained block is byte-identical to origin/main's copy (5599/5599 bytes), and a duplicate-key detector over the whole file at both HEAD and origin/main reports NONE. Nothing else was lost: 19 story budget entries, 45 registered stories, review-replacement-recovery present, zero changed values on any shared key. Remaining config diff vs origin/main is fully accounted for: this Story's budget entry, its registration, current_story_id, and one pure positional shift with identical value. PR shape re-derived at this head: src/ and bin/ diff vs merge-base is EMPTY and 31d84833 is an ancestor of origin/main, so no foreign Story lineage. The diff reads as one intent and the budget-amendment commits are review governance for THIS Story only.

findings.detail: Confirms rather than refutes the previous round. The Story labels split-argument 3 as verified and asserts VET-S-1 is an invariant only satisfiable when deletion and enforcement land at the same HEAD. VET-S-1 as written is a state criterion about file counts, so the deletion-only half would reach that state at its own HEAD; what it genuinely lacks is the enforcement criterion VET-S-5. The section's conclusion survives because argument 2 (the ordering constraint) is independently verified and sufficient alone. Recommend narrowing argument 3's citation from VET-S-1 to VET-S-5. Not blocking, since no gate decision depends on the VET-S-1 framing.

Commit 2f200bf2 is titled 'withdraw two untrue gate observations and de-duplicate config' but git show --stat shows a single tracked file, .vibepro/config.json, 16 deletions. The observation withdrawals live under .vibepro/ paths excluded via .git/info/exclude, so a reviewer reading tracked history alone cannot verify the first half of the claim. Traceability only; recommend future commit messages note explicitly that .vibepro changes are untracked.

inspection.summary: Ran a python json.loads with an object_pairs_hook duplicate-key counter over .vibepro/config.json at HEAD and at git show origin/main version - both NONE. Structurally diffed both configs: per-story budget maps (HEAD 19 / MAIN 18, only-HEAD is this Story, no CHANGED entries), stories arrays (45 vs 44, review-replacement-recovery present), and a full flattened key comparison outside those subtrees showing only brainbase/current_story_id differs. Brace-matched extraction confirmed the retained task-atomic block is byte-identical to main's at 5599 bytes. Ran git log origin/main..HEAD, git diff --name-status, the src/bin merge-base diff, git merge-base --is-ancestor 31d84833 origin/main, git show --stat on 2f200bf2 and b9ed51a3, and node scripts/lint-e2e-product-execution.mjs. Read the Story split rationale and the VET-S-1/VET-S-5 lines. Did not run the unit or e2e suites (forbidden this round).

judgment_delta: Initial: expect the duplicate to be gone but suspect the merge-resolution rewrite silently dropped or reordered other entries, and expect the config/decisions commits to be splittable scope -> Final pass, because the duplicate-key detector reports NONE across the whole file, the byte-identical retained block plus a full flattened key comparison prove no other value was lost or altered, and every remaining difference is this Story's own registration, budget and current_story_id plus one harmless positional shift. The budget amendments and the vacuous-e2e decision records are all this-Story governance with no foreign lineage, so splitting them out would strand the PR's own approval trail.
